title: Kurz und klar: Was du kannst

blocks.title: Was du kannst — Guten Appetit!
bullets: You can name food, drinks, shops and the four moments of the eating day.
You can write a shopping list and invite people to a barbecue with {{de:Kommt ihr?}}
You can buy at a counter: ask a price, order with {{de:möchte}}, take one more item, decline with a reason.
You can read a price tag aloud — {{de:1,09 Euro}} becomes {{de:ein Euro neun}}.
You can put the thing you buy into the accusative: {{de:den Käse}}, {{de:das Brot}}, {{de:die Gurke}}, {{de:die Tomaten}}.
You can conjugate {{de:mögen}} and {{de:möchten}}, and say what you like with {{de:gern}}.
You can move a time word to the front and still keep the verb in position two.
You can read a longer text with the help of Wer?, Was?, Wann?, Wo? and Wie?
You can sort new words into a mindmap and into pairs, so they come back when you need them.

paragraphs.text: Guten Appetit! · Prost! · Mahlzeit! · Was kostet das? · Ich möchte …, bitte. · Sonst noch etwas? · Nein, danke. Ich bin satt. · Ich mag … / Ich esse gern … · Morgens isst Lina Müsli. · Wir grillen heute Abend bei uns. Kommt ihr?

Ten sentences carry most of this lesson: a toast, a price, an order, a refusal, a preference, a statement with the verb in second place, and an invitation. Say them once without looking — if all ten come out, the rest of the chapter will follow.

The habit worth keeping is the one from page 50: file each new word where it belongs, next to the word it keeps company with. Salt with pepper, bread with rolls, and a shopping list with the shop it was written for.
